3.20.3.en: St. Augustine — The wise are united with the Lord Christ, the wisdom of God; in the waters of Baptism they become children of God, and therefore it is said of them that they inherit glory as a personal right of theirs, since they are sons. But the fools deprive themselves of enjoying it, and consequently of partaking in His glory, and so they come into eternal shame.

3.20.4.en: * (The wise) not only receive (glory) but inherit it.

3.20.5.en: Likewise the wicked, even if they become great, become great only to receive a greater dishonor. And just as a man does not honor his wicked colleague if he exalts himself, but rather humiliates him, by declaring his shame before the enemy, so God glorifies the wicked person (for a time) in order to show his shame all the more. Pharaoh (in the days of Moses) became great only so that the world might condemn him.

3.20.7.en: Carry me to You, O Royal Way

3.20.8.en: * Carry me to You, O divine Wisdom; I will walk in You and by You to the bosom of Your Father, turning neither to the right nor to the left.

3.20.9.en: You are the safe Royal Way!

3.20.10.en: * Let me hear Your voice in my depths, and in humility let me bow down to listen to every spiritual counsel.

3.20.11.en: Let me learn obedience that I may be like You. You, the Creator of all, bore obedience to Your Father; carry me, that I may enjoy the fellowship of glorious obedience!

3.20.12.en: By obedience You are pleased with me, and I find favor even in the eyes of men!

3.20.13.en: * On whom shall I lean but on You?!

3.20.14.en: Your bosom is full of tenderness and wisdom!

3.20.15.en: I lean upon it, and my soul is at peace; I rest and enjoy Your leading!

3.20.17.en: Who will give me the spirit of humility?

3.20.18.en: You alone, O Physician of souls and bodies!

3.20.19.en: Let me be humbled, that I may become like an embryo carried in the womb of Your Church, my mother!

3.20.20.en: Through the navel I am nourished by Your precious Blood, and so I am fed and grow and my image is completed.

3.20.21.en: I become in truth Your icon!

3.20.22.en: I bear Your deep humility in my soul!

3.20.23.en: * You have given me Yourself as a way in which I walk.

3.20.24.en: I enter and find You giving even Yourself to Your enemies!

3.20.25.en: Grant me the spirit of giving and generosity, that I may possess You, my precious treasure!

3.20.26.en: * In the midst of the way You chasten me with Your love; You chasten me not to take vengeance on me, but that I may enjoy Your surpassing fatherhood, and that my depths may be renewed and formed by Your Holy Spirit!

3.20.27.en: * Bring me in and hide me in You, that all along the way I may gather the fruits of wisdom with true riches and glory.

3.20.28.en: I enter and feel the warmth of Your love.

3.20.29.en: I walk in safety and assurance.

3.20.30.en: Even in my sleep my dreams, enclosed in You, are sweet to me.

3.20.31.en: * I thank You, O Way, Truth and Love.

3.20.32.en: For as I enjoy Your love, I love every brother and sister of mine.

3.20.33.en: I offer love and kindness with every good thing.

3.20.34.en: I offer my heart, which is Yours, that they may enjoy You.

3.20.35.en: I offer them from what You have given me, O You who are all love and wisdom.

3.20.36.en: So let Your blessing rest upon me in this world!

3.20.37.en: And let me experience the fellowship of Your glory here as in the age to come!

4.0.0.en: 1 Hear, you children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know understanding. 2 For I give you good doctrine, forsake not my law. 3 For I was my father’s son, tender and only beloved in the sight of my mother. 4 He taught me also, and said unto me: Let your heart retain my words: keep my commandments, and live. 5 Get wisdom, get understanding: forget it not; neither decline from the words of my mouth. 6 Forsake her not, and she shall preserve you: love her, and she shall keep you. 7 Wisdom is the head; therefore get wisdom: and with all your getting get understanding. 8 Exalt her, and she shall promote you: she shall bring you to honor, when you embrace her. 9 She shall give to your head an ornament of grace: a crown of beauty shall she deliver to you.

4.0.1.en: The wise Solomon affirms the need to acquire wisdom from God through obedience to the commandment, with prayer and supplication, and the acceptance of the counsel of parents and spiritual leaders, presenting himself as an example to them, as he says:

4.0.2.en: “Hear, you children, the instruction of the Lord, and attend to know understanding.

4.0.3.en: For I give you good doctrine, forsake not my law.

4.0.4.en: For I was my father’s son, tender and only beloved in the sight of my mother” [1-3].

4.0.5.en: The wise Solomon comes to his disciples as to sons of his, so that they may be able to receive his words, which sometimes carry rebuke or reproof. His parents loved him and therefore taught him, and for his part he was attentive and obedient to them. It is as though he says:

4.0.6.en: “What I received from my parents I offer to you. They gave me the teachings of wisdom mingled with love toward me. So listen to me as I listened to them; listen so that you may receive, together with the commandments, fatherly love.”

4.0.7.en: He said this to show them that what he received from his parents and offers to them are exceedingly precious teachings. By this he draws their attention so as to find a way by which he may penetrate to their hearts.

4.0.8.en: The wise Solomon, as a son who obeyed his parents, now teaches his children not by commandments only, but also by his life as an example to them. As St. Athanasius the Apostolic says:

4.0.9.en: * The righteous father brings up (his children) well when he is diligent in teaching others in harmony with his own good conduct, so that he is not ashamed when he hears the objection: “You therefore which teach another, teach you not yourself?!” (Rom 2:21), but rather he is like the good servant who saves himself and wins others. Then the grace he received is doubled, when he hears: “Well done, good and faithful servant: you have been faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things” (Mt 25:21).

4.0.10.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic — The wise man declares that he offers them good doctrine and a law, and as St. Hippolytus says: [It is fitting for us to note that he calls the law a good gift, with regard to the man who takes gifts into his bosom uprightly.]

4.0.11.en: This good doctrine is realized by two things: “hearing the instruction of the Lord,” as though instruction were a teacher to whom we listen, and “attending to know understanding.”

4.0.12.en: “He taught me also, and said unto me:

4.0.13.en: Let your heart retain my words.

4.1.0.en: Forget it not; neither decline from the words of my mouth” [4-5].

4.1.1.en: * By saying, “and I shall live,” he does not ask for ordinary length of life, but asks for a life pleasing to God. Therefore he says: “and I will keep Your words,” because keeping the words of God and doing His commandments are true life and the cause of eternal life.

4.1.2.en: Anthimus, Bishop of Jerusalem — * The word “and I shall live” suggests a movement of life in the future. For I am not thinking of the present life, since he says “I shall live,” and this is certainly in keeping with the true life.

4.1.3.en: Let us hear St. Paul as he speaks of himself and those like him: “Our life is hid with Christ in God. When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall you also appear with Him in glory” (cf. Col 3:3).

4.1.4.en: Let us understand “I shall live” as belonging to the future, and also “I hide Your word,” that this will be a reality, not in a mirror nor in an enigma.

4.1.5.en: Origen, the scholar — * I do not feel that I fulfill Your commandments without reward; give us the reward of this: a happy, immortal life that I may live and keep Your words.

4.1.6.en: St. Didymus the Blind — * Who can deny that the gift of life is a work of divine majesty? It is written: “Quicken Your servant.” Thus He gives life to one who is a servant, that is, man, who had no life before, but received it as a gift to him.

4.2.0.en: St. Ambrose — “Forsake her not, and she shall preserve you: love her, and she shall keep you” [6].

4.2.1.en: By saying “forsake her not,” he personifies wisdom, presenting her as a guardian and friend, for if you do not forsake her, she remains faithful in guarding you, and if you love her, she undertakes to protect you.

4.2.2.en: When St. Gregory of Nyssa speaks to virgins of both sexes, he asks them to accept the counsel of the wise Solomon, so that they love wisdom as a helper and companion to them, for she also gives love as the wedding garment without which the wedding of the soul with the Lord Christ will not take place. He sees in divine wisdom a Bridegroom for the soul, who satisfies its depths and fills it with joy.

4.2.3.en: * If a man accepts the advice of Solomon and cares for the helper and companion, that is, true wisdom, of whom it was said: “love her, and she shall keep you,” “honor her, and she shall embrace you,” by this he prepares himself in a fitting way for such love, so that he may celebrate the wedding with the consecrated guests, wearing a garment without stain. Then he is not cast out when he sits at the celebration for not having put on the wedding garment.

4.2.4.en: It is also clear that what is said here concerns men and women on an equal footing, that they may move toward the wedding.

4.2.5.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa — “Wisdom is the head (the foundation); therefore get wisdom: and with all your getting get understanding” [6].

4.2.6.en: Christ, the Head of the Church and her Foundation, is Wisdom; whoever acquires Him enjoys wisdom and understanding, where he grasps the surpassing mysteries of God and His plan for our salvation.

4.2.7.en: Let us acquire wisdom as the foundation for building the Kingdom of Heaven within us. She is our eternal treasure, our lasting account, and the cause of fellowship in heavenly glory.

4.2.8.en: How different our wisdom and understanding are from the wisdom and understanding of the wicked! For our wisdom is based on living, practical faith, while the wicked may have faith with theoretical knowledge, but they do not bear the experience of union with God in His Son by the Holy Spirit, the practical living faith through which we practice our true sonship to God.

4.2.9.en: When the Lord Christ becomes our Head, and He is the divine Wisdom, He takes over the leadership of our life, and we practice wisdom in our worship in church as in our private room, in our work as on the road, in our dealings with loved ones as with opponents, in our fellowship with the heavenly ones as with the believers who are still striving... The Lord Christ governs all our aspirations, our glances and our conduct, even our dreams! We see everything through Him, and we see Him transfigured before us in everything.

4.3.0.en: “Exalt her, and she shall promote you: she shall bring you to honor, when you embrace her” [8-9].

4.3.1.en: Some see that the word “exalt” here means “strengthen.” If wisdom is a free divine gift, and is the possession of the Lord Christ Himself, the wisdom of God, then He does not dwell in a slack or careless heart, but He strengthens His dwelling in us by living striving and the enjoyment of holy virtues, that we may embrace Him not with mere words but with practical, living love. We exalt wisdom and strengthen her in us, as the virtues surround her on every side, and then wisdom exalts us and strengthens us. She exalts us in the eyes of God as in the eyes of the heavenly and the earthly, so that even the demons fear us, for we are hidden in Christ, the true Wisdom.

4.3.2.en: * What does “exalt her (strengthen her)” mean? That is, fence her around with holy thoughts, for you need a strong defense, where there are many things exposed to danger, like possessions. But if it is in your power to exalt her, and if it is within your ability to practice virtues that honor the knowledge of God, these become fortresses for her. As an example, whoever maintains the practice (of virtue), the love of study and the rest of the chain of virtues honors wisdom, and the reward is that you are honored by clinging to her and embracing her in the splendor of heaven.

4.3.3.en: St. Hippolytus — * Philosophy was a preparation, making ready the way for him who becomes perfect in Christ. Solomon says: “Exalt her, and she shall promote you: she shall bring you to honor, when you embrace her. She shall give to your head an ornament of grace: a crown of beauty shall she deliver to you” [8-9]. When wisdom is strengthened with the garment of philosophy and by good use, you protect her from the attack of the sophists.

4.4.0.en: St. Clement of Alexandria — “She shall give to your head an ornament of grace: a crown of beauty shall she deliver to you” [9].

4.4.1.en: Wisdom makes of the believer a prince or a king who bears on his head a crown of grace and fellowship in glory, and he sings, saying: “[He] has made us kings and priests unto God and His Father” (Rev 1:8), or she makes of the soul a queen crowned with surpassing heavenly glory and beauty.

4.5.s.en: 2. Wisdom and the life of uprightness

4.5.0.en: 10 Hear, O my son, and receive my sayings; and the years of your life shall be many. 11 I have taught you in the way of wisdom; I have led you in right paths. 12 When you go, your steps shall not be straitened; and when you run, you shall not stumble. 13 Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; for she is your life.

4.5.1.en: The wise Solomon speaks of the positive way of wisdom, saying:

4.5.2.en: “Hear, O my son, and receive my sayings; and the years of your life shall be many” [10].

4.5.3.en: Listening to holy counsel is the beginning of the positive way of wisdom, where in a spirit of humility the believer obeys, walking in the commandment. The fruit of this way is “many years of life,” or length of days. This is a general principle or general fruit, which cannot be applied literally to all believers, since some children and youths were martyred in the prime of their lives, yet they did not die, for they are still in Paradise practicing worship and interceding for the salvation of the world. The saying here is entirely true if taken in the spiritual sense.

4.5.4.en: As for the literal side, we know that evils in general, especially anger, adultery and the like, affect a person’s bodily and psychological health besides the spiritual, which makes him lose his inner peace and exposes him to many diseases. Even if his life on earth is long, it is counted as nothing. But from wisdom springs harmony between body, soul and spirit, so that the person walks with moderation and a spirit of balance, which gives him resistance against many diseases. Sound, living and practical faith is a powerful master not of the spirit alone but also of the body as well as of the psychological side.

4.6.0.en: “I have taught you in the way of wisdom; I have led you in right paths [11].

4.6.1.en: In tender fatherhood Solomon comes to his hearers as a teacher and guide, opening the inner eyes of his disciples so that they may see the way of truth, and taking them by the hand to lead them into the paths of uprightness. In this he bears a shadow of the work of the Lord Christ, whom the Fathers of Alexandria like to call “the Teacher” or “the Trainer.” St. Clement of Alexandria recorded for us a book on this matter which he called “The Trainer, Paedagogos,” in which he showed how the whole world needs the Lord Christ as teacher and physician, and that He leads His believers in the way of perfection until they bear His image in themselves. He taught humanity by His Incarnation, His dwelling in their midst and His crucifixion, that they might know Him and possess Him, and He renews their nature by His Holy Spirit.

4.6.2.en: The Scripture presents various examples of teachers, among them: 1. The prophet Moses: the first leader of the people of God, who taught the people of God the divine law, and asked fathers and mothers to teach their children (Deut 4:5). The living leader creates living leaders, and each generation asks the next to lead those who come after it. 2. Bezalel and Aholiab: two skilled and gifted craftsmen who were called to teach others the making of the tabernacle (Ex 35:30-35); the skilled leader is the one who trains others to become skilled and to work with him. 3. The prophet Samuel: the last judge of the people of Israel before the establishment of the monarchy, who counted slackness in prayer and in teaching the people to be a sin against God Himself, for he says: “Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way” (1 Sam 12:23). 4. David: he was not able to build the temple, but he prepared his son Solomon to build the temple and to set up its furnishings (1 Chr 28:9-21); the teacher or leader is the one who rejoices in the success and growth of his disciples more than in his own. 5. Solomon: known for the wisdom he received as a gift from God, which he used to teach his people to be wise in everything. 6. Ezra: a scribe and priest who was committed not only to keeping the Law but also to teaching it to others (Ezra 7:10). 7. Barnabas: one of the teachers among the believers of Antioch (Acts 13:1), who had an effective influence on Saul of Tarsus after his acceptance of the faith (Acts 9:26-30). 8. Gamaliel: a famous Jewish rabbi, who was the teacher of Saul of Tarsus in his youth and had an influence on him in living according to the Law literally, until he met the Lord Christ and realized the need for a new spiritual view of the Law. 9. Paul: perhaps the most effective teacher of the early Church because of his extraordinary gifts. He taught in the Roman world and confronted philosophical ideas, especially Greek. 10. Priscilla and Aquila: a family who turned their house into a church, and taught a gifted, eloquent young man named Apollos the way of the Lord (Acts 18:20). 11. Apollos: a teacher of powerful influence, an Alexandrian, whose teachings paved the way for the acceptance of the Gospel in Ephesus (Acts 18:24-26). 12. Timothy: a young man whom St. Paul led to Christianity, who became a bishop (1 Tim 1:3; 2 Tim 4:2). 13. Titus: another young man whom St. Paul also led to Christianity and who became bishop of the Church in Crete (Titus 2:1-15).

4.7.0.en: “When you go, your steps shall not be straitened; and when you run, you shall not stumble” [12].

4.7.1.en: When the believer bears wisdom within him, he walks in his daily life with a spirit of clarity and uprightness, without fear of the future. Therefore we find him, not only in his worship but also in his daily work, walking with wide steps, working without ceasing, running with joy under the shadow of God’s surpassing care.

4.7.2.en: Walking with wide steps and running without stumbling carry the upright conduct, where the believer knows neither malice nor deceit, and does not waste his time or his work in crooked ways.

4.8.0.en: “Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; for she is your life” [13].

4.8.1.en: By instruction (discipline) is meant not merely good conduct, or nobility in dealing with others, but clinging to the Lord Himself. What the wise Solomon says here he repeats in the Song of Songs in the voice of the bride, who held her heavenly Bridegroom and did not let him go until she brought him into the depths of her soul and was united with him (Song 3:4).

4.9.s.en: 3. Guarding oneself against the wicked and evil

4.9.0.en: 14 Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil men. 15 Avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, and pass away. 16 For they sleep not, except they have done mischief; and their sleep is taken away, unless they cause some to fall. 17 For they eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of injustice. 18 But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shines more and more unto the perfect day. 19 The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble. 20 My son, attend to my words; incline your ear unto my sayings. 21 Let them not depart from your eyes; keep them in the midst of your heart. 22 For they are life unto those that find them, and medicine to all the body. 23 Keep your heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life. 24 Put away from you a froward mouth, and put far from you perverse lips. 25 Let your eyes look right on, and let your eyelids look straight before you. 26 Make level the path of your feet, and let all your ways be established. 27 Turn not to the right hand nor to the left: remove your foot from evil.

4.9.1.en: After speaking about the positive side of the way of wisdom, the wise man speaks to us about the negative side, which is guarding oneself against the wicked and evil.

4.9.2.en: The wise captain of a ship does not have complete familiarity with all the rocks of the ocean and the reefs and the dangerous regions, but he studies with all precision the straight course, and knows its directions, and understands its details, and so he sails with assurance. So the man of God turns aside from the rugged ways of the wicked, and does not waste his time being occupied with them, but is occupied with the way of truth, and knows its features and all its details as he walks in it with assurance.

4.9.3.en: “Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil men.

4.9.5.en: Pass not by it, turn from it, and pass away” [14-15].

4.9.6.en: Let us flee from clinging to the wicked in their sinful conduct. Let us avoid their ways, and not flatter them at the expense of our salvation, but let our souls be earnest in closing every door that leads us into sin. Let us not pass along with the wicked in their way out of courtesy to them, or out of a desire to satisfy bodily lusts or to obtain material or moral gains. If we notice that we have come near to it, let us turn our back to it and return from it, clinging to the Lord. Let us pass away from it quickly so that we do not fall into snares.

4.9.7.en: St. Hippolytus sees that the wise man advises us to keep away from the way of the heretics who in their wickedness corrupt the teachings, as well as from those who are perverse in their conduct, whom he calls the evil men.

4.9.8.en: * The heretics are “the wicked,” and those who rebel against the Law are the evil men; he commands us to keep away from their ways, which are their works.

4.9.9.en: St. Hippolytus — Since the way of the heretics is shining with vain philosophies, and the way of the evil men is also alluring with its bodily pleasures and its material and moral gains, therefore the wise man powerfully asks us not merely to keep some distance away from these ways, but to turn our backs on them completely. For the way of the righteousness of Christ is light, while the way of evil and iniquity is darkness; and there is no fellowship between light and darkness, between righteousness and corruption, between truth and falsehood.

4.9.10.en: We need a leader who directs our life in a direction opposed to evil, namely the Holy Spirit, the Spirit of Christ, who is able to carry us to where Christ is seated!

4.9.11.en: The wise man continues his speech about the wicked, saying:

4.10.0.en: “For they sleep not, except they have done mischief; and their sleep is taken away, unless they cause some to fall” [16].

4.10.1.en: The heretics, and likewise the evil men, do not rest until they ensnare as many souls as they can in the snares of heresies or the nets of corruption. They spend the nights of their lives without sleep in order to push every person they can toward their way.

4.11.0.en: “For they eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of injustice” [17].

4.11.1.en: Their food is stolen bread, and their drink is the wine of violence. Two characteristics accompany the wicked: theft or dishonesty, and violence or injustice. Here he does not mean theft in its narrow sense, for the wicked person may embezzle the glory of God or rob the truth by distorting its image. As for injustice, they sometimes present it through sweet words full of gentleness and kindness in appearance.

4.12.0.en: “But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shines more and more unto the perfect day. The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble” [18-19].

4.12.1.en: The upright way is distinct from the sinful way. The first way leads to the high city of God, where the Lamb of God, who lights it, is found; therefore the way is radiant and bright, bearing rays of heavenly glory with which it enlightens the minds of those who walk in it, so that they say: “Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his!” (Num 23:10). But the way of the wicked bears the marks of its end, namely the kingdom of darkness.

4.12.2.en: The word “path” came in the plural in the Septuagint: “the paths of the just.” If the truth is one way, the Person of the Lord Christ, He draws believers to Himself by many ways. Truly all must have one faith, but each has his own gift. One person meets the Lord with a spirit of constant worship, another with a spirit of love and giving to others, and a third with a spirit of service and preaching, as St. Paul the Apostle says: “There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit. And there are differences of ministries, but the same Lord. And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God who works all in all. But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all: for to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom; to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit...” (1 Cor 12:4-9).

4.12.3.en: * The way of truth is one, but in it is an ever-flowing river, from which streams overflow on every side. Therefore the inspired word says: Hear, O my son, and receive my sayings, and you shall have many ways of life. I have taught you in the way of wisdom, so your springs will not run dry, those that overflow from the earth itself. There are not only various ways of salvation which the righteous man uses, but (God) adds many other ways for the righteous, for he says: “The paths of the just are as the shining light” [18].

4.12.4.en: St. Clement of Alexandria — When St. John Cassian spoke about our imitating others, he warned us against being attached to one person, since there is no perfect person in whom are all the virtues.

4.12.5.en: The wise man likens the paths of the just to the earth upon which the Sun of Righteousness has shone, and which continues to send forth its rays until the light increases and reaches the peak. But the way of the wicked is one from which the Sun of Righteousness is hidden, therefore darkness prevails over it, and those who walk in it stumble.

4.12.6.en: * He says: “Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven” (Mt 5:16). Nothing is so full of light as the most exalted conversation. And as one of the wise says: “The paths of the just are as the shining light” (Prov 4:18) LXX, and they shine not for themselves alone, kindling the flame of their (illuminating) works, and not only for the sake of righteousness, but they also shine upon their relatives.

4.12.7.en: St. John Chrysostom — “My son, attend to my words; incline your ear unto my sayings.

4.12.8.en: Let them not depart from your eyes; keep them in the midst of your heart.

4.13.0.en: For they are life unto those that find them, and medicine to all the body” [20-22].

4.13.1.en: The wise man returns to ask his son to consecrate all the members of his body and his energies to the enjoyment of wisdom, so he asks him to incline his ears, and to look to her with his eyes continually, and to bring her into the depths of his heart. He asks him to store her in the midst of his heart so that she may move all his energies, desires, longings, words and conduct.

4.14.0.en: “Keep your heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life” [23].

4.14.1.en: Just as impure blood enters the heart and then leaves it purified through the arteries to nourish the whole body from the top of the head to the soles of the feet, so the righteousness of Christ enters the depths of the heart to crown the whole inner and outer being of man.

4.14.2.en: What we keep in our heart reigns over our thoughts, our words and our conduct, whether it is the righteousness of Christ or evil.

4.14.3.en: * Let us keep our hearts, and let us keep our mouths, for it is written of both. In this place we are commanded to beware of our mouth, and in another place it was said to you: “Keep your heart with all diligence.” If David takes heed, will you not take heed?!

4.14.4.en: If Isaiah had unclean lips, for he said: “Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips” (Isa 6:5); if the prophet of the Lord had unclean lips, how shall we have clean lips?

4.14.5.en: St. Ambrose — * Keep your heart with all diligence, that is, not in secret, for thoughts must be shown and works revealed. Use your hands in work, and your heart in meditation in prayer.

4.14.6.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian — * Let us be on our guard with all care, as it is written: “Keep your heart with all vigilance.” For our enemies are fearsome and crafty, the evil spirits, against whom we wrestle, and as the Apostle says, we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. How many they are in the air around us! For they are not far from us.

4.15.s.en: King Solomon and the scientist Harvey

4.15.0.en: Some see in the saying of the wise Solomon, “Keep your heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life” [23], that he preceded the scientist Harvey, who made the great discovery of the circulation of the blood that is accomplished by the heart; this discovery which brought about a revolution in medical thought. Here we find Solomon speaking calmly and with certainty, using this scientific fact to reveal a spiritual truth. Just as the heart is the center of the bodily system, from which life issues, so the heart, or the inner man, is the center of the spiritual life1.

4.16.0.en: “Put away from you a froward mouth, and put far from you perverse lips” [24].

4.16.1.en: What is a froward mouth but anger, condemnation and rashness in speech, while perverse lips mean slander and the distortion of facts.

4.16.2.en: “Let your eyes look right on (uprightly), and let your eyelids look straight before you.

4.17.0.en: Make level the path of your feet, and let all your ways be established” [25-26].

4.17.1.en: The work of the men of the Old Testament was to prepare the way so that believers might walk it with a spirit of strength and victory, with souls strengthened by the spirit of living hope. St. John the Baptist, who came in the spirit of Elijah to prepare the way for the Lord, cried out, saying: “Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make His paths straight. Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough ways shall be made smooth; and all flesh shall see the salvation of God” (Lk 3:4-6).

4.17.2.en: Thus the wise Solomon shares with the rest of the men of the Old Testament in preparing humanity to receive the Lord, so that it may walk in straight paths with strong feet able to cross the Royal Way, in which you never find a lame person! He does not walk it who limps between God and Belial, nor between fervent spirituality and deadly literalism, nor between heaven and earth, but in it the Gospel of Christ, the Giver of heavenly joy, is revealed!

4.17.3.en: * For the sake of learning, it was well said of Solomon: “My son, do nothing without counsel, and when it is accomplished you will not regret it” (Sir 32:24). And also: “Let your eyelids be before your steps” [25]. For truly our eyelids go before our steps when good counsels govern our actions. For he who neglects to look ahead, and closes his eyes when he wants to go forward to work during his journey, does not go forward to work looking ahead, and so soon falls, since he does not take heed with the eyelids of the eye of counsel to perceive where he must place the foot of his knowledge.

4.17.5.en: * He whose thoughts are free from passion looks uprightly, and his judgment is sound, not swayed by outward appearances. When he says, “Let your eyes look right on,” he means the insight of the soul.

4.17.6.en: St. Hippolytus — Finally the wise man says:

4.18.0.en: “Turn not to the right hand nor to the left: remove your foot from evil” [27].

4.18.1.en: He warns us against walking in crooked and deviating ways, whether on the right side or the left, for the straight Royal Way is the way of moderation.

4.18.2.en: * It is truly fitting for us to walk the Royal Way and not to deviate to one side of it, whether to the right or to the left, as the Book of Proverbs says.

4.18.3.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus — * Solomon, the wisest of men, warns us not to deviate to the right side or the left side. So do not exalt yourself because of your virtues, nor be puffed up because of the spiritual heights you have reached, deviating toward the right. And do not sway toward the way of vices, toward the left, boasting of what is shameful (Phil 3:19).

4.18.4.en: St. Hippolytus — * Virtue occupies a middle position; it is said that mature courage is the way between recklessness and cowardice.

4.18.5.en: St. John Cassian — * Deviation to the right is that a person deceives himself and says that he is without sin. And deviation to the left is that a man surrounds himself with his sins, thinking that he will suffer no harm and will not be punished.

4.18.6.en: St. Augustine — And in the discourse of St. John Cassian on “how vainglory attacks the monk from the right and from the left,” he says:

4.18.7.en: * Whoever aspires to go forward on the Royal Way “by the armor of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,” must, according to the teaching of the Apostle, pass “by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report” (2 Cor 6:7, 8).

4.18.8.en: He proceeds carefully to direct his straight course amid the tossing waves of trials. And with caution he holds the rudder, so he gives the Spirit of the Lord, and spreads His fragrance around us.

4.18.9.en: We know that if we deviate a little to the right or the left, the ship of our life is soon shattered upon the rugged rocks. Therefore the wise Solomon warns us, saying: “Turn not to the right hand nor to the left” (Prov 4:27). That is, do not praise your virtues before yourself, nor boast of your spiritual achievements on the right, nor turn to the way of vices toward the left, choosing for yourself some of these vices, using the words of the Apostle: “glorying in your shame” (Phil 3:19).

4.18.10.en: For when the devil cannot stir up vainglory in a man by means of his good appearance and the elegance of his dress, he tries to produce it by means of unkempt garb and dirty, neglected clothing.

4.18.11.en: And if he cannot make a man fall by pride, he makes him fall by humility.

4.18.12.en: And if he cannot drive him toward self-exaltation by the grace of knowledge and eloquence, he drags him down under the weight of silence.

4.18.13.en: And if a man fasts openly, the pride of conceit and vanity attacks him, and if he hides it, scorning the boasting it brings, he falls prey to the very sin of pride.

4.18.14.en: And so that the stain of vainglory may not drive him, he avoids prolonging his prayers in the sight of the brethren, but because he practices them in secret, with no one noticing him, he does not escape the pride of conceit.

4.18.16.en: Carry me in the way of wisdom
